subject: Coffee & Tea
title: First Crack and Second Crack
description: A micro-lesson that makes First Crack and Second Crack usable.

hook.text: During roasting, coffee beans literally crack—twice. Each crack signals a critical chemical milestone.

buildup.text: First crack happens around 196°C. Steam pressure inside the bean breaks the cell structure. It sounds like popcorn.

discovery.text: After first crack, origin flavors emerge: fruit, floral, citrus. This is where light roasts stop.

twist.text: Second crack occurs near 224°C as oils migrate to the surface. The bean darkens and smoky flavors dominate.

climax.text: Past second crack, roast flavors overpower origin. Dark roasts taste more like the roast than the bean.

punchline.text: Two cracks, two choices. Origin flavor or roast flavor.

quiz.question: What happens at first crack during coffee roasting?
options: Steam pressure breaks cell structure, releasing origin flavors
